d: The main estrogen after menopause, made when aromatase in adipose tissue converts androstenedione from the adrenal glands and ovarian stroma. More body fat means more estrone and a higher endometrial cancer risk.
The Stages of Reproductive Aging Workshop system, which divides reproductive life into reproductive, menopausal transition and postmenopausal stages anchored to the final menstrual period, stage 0.
Loss of ovarian function before age 40, with amenorrhea and a high FSH on two occasions. Causes include Turner syndrome, the fragile X premutation, autoimmunity, chemotherapy and radiation.

Hypothalamic neurons that release kisspeptin, neurokinin B and dynorphin. Estrogen restrains them; after menopause they become overactive, drive GnRH pulses and signal through NK3 receptors to cause hot flashes.

Vaginal and urinary symptoms of estrogen loss: dryness, painful intercourse, urgency and recurrent urinary infections, caused by a thin, glycogen-poor epithelium and a rising vaginal pH. Low-dose vaginal estrogen treats it.

Processing of a swallowed drug by the liver before it reaches the systemic circulation. Oral estrogen's first pass raises clotting factors, triglycerides and binding globulins; transdermal estradiol avoids it.

Large randomized trials begun in the 1990s that gave oral conjugated estrogen with or without medroxyprogesterone to postmenopausal women aged 50 to 79 and found more stroke, clots and, with the combined regimen, breast cancer.
